what: The photo looks as if seen through vertical grooved glass (8 strips) — clear when the cursor is inside the photo, and the farther it moves sideways, the more each groove shifts the photo into stripes while the groove band flows toward the cursor (following .25s late). Leaving only above or below splits it halfway. On touch devices the photo is clear at screen center and splits toward the top and bottom ends.

options.amount: Cursor distance (in photo-width units) × this value is the displacement strength, default 60
options.touch: Touch-device screen slot (center 0 · ends ±.5) × this value, default 130
options.follow: Seconds for intensity to follow, default .25
options.band: Width of one groove band set (ratio of photo width), default .4
options.stretch: Ratio by which the photo stretches horizontally with intensity, default .05
options.[data-fx-part=source]: Warp photo — img, canvas and video (children, required). Being WebGL, only same-origin images work (img on file:// is blocked — draw it with canvas or serve it over http)

note: The original lays the home image (jpg) as a repeating map on a PixiJS 8 DisplacementFilter (scale x 100·y .5) — the map is rebuilt in the same form (horizontal slope per row). When the photo slot size changes, it is refitted with a ResizeObserver. Drawing stops when off-screen (20% margin above and below).

from.where: shared.js slitGlass (the two journey photos on the first page — cursor distance ×60 · .25s power1.out · phone uses scroll position ×130. The About page message video applies the same filter by scroll position only)
